pairs_touching.homonym_positive_evidence: Different responsibility with no continuity, explicitly recorded: BC-7 (Grant-record) owns only record-schema/registration; the performative Human Act itself is explicitly excluded and owned by a different bounded context (Knowledge Engineering/Governance). No lineage claim shows one deriving from or extending the other.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Shared rows S0067/S0071 record an explicit DDD boundary decision: 'Human Act is rejected as aggregate root... it has neither identity nor lifecycle inside BC-7, and promoting it would duplicate a concept another (Knowledge Engineering/Governance) context owns'; 'BC-7 owns only the requirement that an act be recorded..., never the performative act itself, which exists outside the software.' This is different-responsibility-with-no-continuity: Grant-record and Human-Act are ruled to be two separate concepts owned by different bounded contexts.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a later row reversed this and merged Human-Act into Grant-record's own aggregate, REPLACEMENT or REDEFINITION would fit better than HOMONYM; no such reversal was found in the sampled/shared rows.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both are documented as the two halves of the same constitutional Article 3 (Authority): S0237's Family 3 (AUTHORITY) table lists 'INV-003 Assessment != Authority... an instance of Relation-001' alongside 'Authority-as-Recorded-Reference' (human-act's content) side by side; S0241 (Article 3) states both clauses together: 'evidence/assessment/source SHALL NOT constitute authority; authority SHALL be assigned -- a recorded reference to a human act.' human-act rows (S0172/S0188/S0234) supply the positive mechanism (grants reference a human act) that completes what INV-003's negative boundary (Assessment != Authority) leaves open.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row showing human-act and INV-003 address unrelated constitutional concerns rather than jointly composing Article 3's Authority clause (e.g. if human-act's grant-reference mechanism has no connection to the Assessment/Authority boundary).
